assessment.summary: An ongoing, human-caused warming of the climate system with civilizational-scale risks under continued high emissions. NOAA reports record October 2026 temperature departures and a second-warmest January–October period; atmospheric CO2 continues to rise year over year.
assessment.timeframe: Already underway; impacts intensify with cumulative emissions.

claims.text: The IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report attributes approximately 1.1 °C of global warming since 1850-1900 to human activities.

NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information ranked 2025 as the third-warmest year in the global temperature record dating back to 1850: the annual global surface temperature was 2.11°F (1.17°C) above the 20th-century average and 2.41°F (1.34°C) above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial average, behind only 2024 and 2023. The ten warmest years in the 176-year record have all occurred since 2015, and upper-ocean heat content was record high in 2025.
NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory measured a monthly mean atmospheric CO2 concentration of 426.07 ppm at Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii in September 2026, up from 424.37 ppm in September 2025.

NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information reported that global surface temperatures in July 2026 were 2.12°F (1.18°C) above the 20th-century average, tying with 2024 for the warmest July on record, and that the January-July global surface temperature was the third highest on record. NCEI's annual outlook states it is very likely that 2026 will rank among the five-warmest years on record, with the highest probabilities favoring it as the third- or fourth-warmest.

NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information reported that the September 2026 global surface temperature was 2.39°F (1.33°C) above the 20th-century average, the second-warmest September in the 1850-2026 record, trailing 2023 by 0.13°F (0.07°C), and that the January-September global surface temperature was the second highest on record behind 2024. NCEI states it is very likely that 2026 will rank among the five-warmest years on record, with the highest probabilities favouring 2026 as the second-warmest year on record.

NOAA reports that October 2026 global surface temperature was 1.43°C above the 20th-century average, the largest monthly departure in its 1850–2026 record. January–October ranked second warmest at 1.20°C above average, behind 2024; its annual outlook favors 2026 finishing second warmest. The October ocean surface temperature departure reached 1.14°C above average, also a record for any month.

description: Human greenhouse-gas emissions are warming Earth's climate, with widespread effects on weather extremes, sea levels and ecosystems. NOAA reports that October 2026 set a monthly global temperature-departure record at 1.43°C above the 20th-century average. January–October ranked second warmest, and its annual outlook favors a second-place finish. These anomalies use a different baseline from pre-industrial warming estimates. Mauna Loa CO2 averaged 426.07 ppm in September 2026, up from 424.37 ppm a year earlier. Upper-ocean heat content reached a record in 2025 for the fifth consecutive year.
name: Climate Change (Global Warming)
